_meta.description: Plain-English definitions for every finance term and abbreviation used in the Deal Economics Copilot UI and outputs. No unexplained jargon anywhere in the product (KICKOFF §9.7).

terms.ASP: Average selling price — the per-unit price a GPU is sold for before rebates or other reductions.
terms.COGS: Cost of goods sold — the per-unit cost to build and deliver a GPU; gross revenue minus COGS is gross margin.
terms.Gross margin: Net revenue minus COGS, shown in dollars and as a percent of net revenue; the deal's core profitability before allocated operating expense.
terms.Net revenue: Gross revenue minus rebates and (under GAAP) minus warrant contra-revenue; the revenue actually recognized.
terms.Contribution margin: Gross margin minus allocated operating expense — what the deal contributes after its share of opex.
terms.NPV: Net present value — future cash flows discounted to today at the WACC; positive means the deal creates value. Here it is pre-tax operating NPV.
terms.WACC: Weighted average cost of capital — the annual discount rate used for NPV; owned by Treasury.
terms.Payback: The quarter at which a deal's cumulative discounted cash flow first turns non-negative — when it has paid back its investment.
terms.Take-or-pay: A clause requiring the buyer to pay for a minimum volume even if it takes less; the shortfall is invoiced, protecting the seller's revenue floor.
terms.Banked Units: Units paid for under take-or-pay but not taken; they may be drawn down in a later period of higher demand, and are forfeited if unused at term end.
terms.Rebate: A volume discount credited back to the buyer once cumulative purchases cross a tier threshold; reduces net revenue.
terms.Prepayment: An upfront customer payment recorded as a contract liability and drawn down against future invoices (here, 20% of each invoice until exhausted).
terms.Contract liability: Deferred revenue — cash received before the related goods are delivered; the prepayment balance is a contract liability.
terms.MFN: Most-favored-nation clause — a promise not to sell to a comparable-volume customer at a lower price; can trigger repricing exposure across the portfolio.
terms.Contra-revenue: A reduction of revenue (not an expense). Equity given to a customer (a warrant) is consideration payable to a customer, recorded as contra-revenue under ASC 606.
terms.Warrant: A right granted to the customer to buy the seller's stock at a fixed price; its fair value is a cost to the seller, recorded as contra-revenue.
terms.Dilution: The increase in shares outstanding (and reduction in existing holders' ownership %) if warrant shares are issued.
terms.Effective net ASP: The all-in per-unit price after subtracting rebates and warrant cost from the sticker ASP — what the seller really nets per GPU.
terms.Accrual: Recognizing an expense or liability as it is incurred rather than when paid; the rebate accrual builds a liability each quarter at the expected blended rate.
terms.DSO: Days sales outstanding — how long after billing a customer pays; longer DSO ties up more working capital in receivables.
terms.DPO: Days payable outstanding — how long the seller takes to pay its suppliers; longer DPO frees up working capital.
terms.Inventory lead: Months that inventory (component) cash is funded ahead of the shipment it supports; the ramp's inventory build is a working-capital draw.
terms.Working capital: Cash tied up in the operating cycle — receivables and inventory, net of payables; the peak draw is the most cash the deal ties up before turning cash-positive.
terms.Peak receivables: The largest accounts-receivable balance the deal reaches, driven by the billing ramp and DSO; the working-capital float of the payment terms.
terms.PUE: Power usage effectiveness — the ratio of total data-center power to IT power; used in the capacity bridge to convert gigawatts to GPU units.
terms.Capacity bridge: The conversion from a power commitment (gigawatts) to a GPU unit count, using power per GPU and PUE.
terms.Tornado: A one-way sensitivity chart ranking inputs by their dollar impact on gross margin, widest bar at the top.
terms.Scenario: A modeled case (BASE, DOWNSIDE take-or-pay, UPSIDE volume, EARLY_TERMINATION); each is run under both GAAP and cash views.
terms.GAAP view: The accounting view of revenue, including warrant contra-revenue.
terms.Cash / commercial view: The cash view of the deal, excluding the non-cash warrant contra-revenue.
terms.Variance bridge: A driver-level walk from one deal version to another, attributing the dollar change in a metric to each term/assumption that moved; the steps sum exactly to the total delta.
terms.Goal-seek: Solving for the input value (e.g. ASP) that hits a target metric (e.g. 45% gross margin), by deterministic bisection over the engine.
terms.CRB: Contract Review Board — the approval meeting where a deal's economics and risks are challenged; the policy engine encodes its rules.
terms.Policy verdict: The CRB engine's output for a deal: pass / escalate / block per rule, plus the required approver list and reasons.
terms.Assumption Register: The single list of every model input, classified by type (contract fact / market data / policy number / strategic judgment) with the owner who confirms it.
terms.Assumption Gap Report: Ranked clarifying questions for the deal team, each with the dollar sensitivity of the unknown and the owner who resolves it.
terms.Provenance: Where an assumption came from — contract, term sheet, library default, placeholder, or user override — surfaced as a badge in the UI and Excel.
terms.ASC 606: The revenue-recognition standard; under it, consideration payable to a customer (a warrant) reduces the transaction price as contra-revenue.
terms.ASC 718: The stock-compensation standard used to measure the fair value of the warrant granted to the customer.
terms.Liquidated damages: Pre-agreed amounts payable for a breach such as a delivery slip (e.g. a per-week penalty capped at a percentage), avoiding a dispute over actual loss.
